The XML declares a single MIME-type element for the `nxm` scheme with a `<glob-deleteall/>` instruction (which simply removes any inherited globs so only the application-registered patterns match). This is a routine, legitimate practice for desktop applications that want to handle their own custom URL schemes (e.g., `nxm://...`).

There are no network requests, downloads, eval/obfuscation, unexpected file operations, or any other indicators of malicious behavior. The file is consistent with ordinary packaging of an application that registers a custom scheme handler. Note that `glob-deleteall` combined with no globs listed means the handler is registered but does not match file extensions — this is a minor packaging consideration, not a security threat.
